title: An intermediate gyration maximizes how closely Anthrobots track scratch edges

fields.label: Label
fields.value: An intermediate gyration maximizes how closely Anthrobots track scratch edges

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In a constrained set of 13 Anthrobots in neuronal scratches, gyration (rotational tendency) has a quadratic relationship with how closely a bot's trajectory follows the scratch edge (p = 0.006), suggesting an intermediate gyration range maximizes edge tracking.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: With our constrained dataset, we saw that gyration had a quadratic effect on scratch‐trajectory similarity (Figure 5E) with p = 0.006, suggesting that there is a specific range for gyration where the scratch‐trajectory correlation can be maximized

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro”. Scope: 13 NHBE-derived Anthrobots with rotational tendency 0.33–0.7 in hiNSC-derived neuronal scratches

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-19: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mathematical relationship is directly testable, but available coverage is extremely small and post hoc filtered. Existing data can reproduce the reported association without robustly establishing a general maximizing range.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit prespecified linear and quadratic models to gyration and scratch-trajectory similarity for all eligible bots and evaluate the estimated optimum with cross-validation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Only 13 selected observations define the apparent optimum.

The quadratic model was chosen after residual inspection.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.28
analysis feasibility: 0.87
data existence: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.96
discriminating power: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A quadratic versus linear comparison of gyration against edge-tracking is a definite statistical claim. The paper reports p = 0.006 on a constrained set of 13 bots and does not release the points. With that sample size and with the model chosen after inspecting residuals, the open record cannot show whether an interior maximum is real.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On the pre-specified gyration window, fit scratch-edge similarity as a quadratic function of gyration and compare it with a linear fit on the same 13 bots. A quadratic improvement with an interior maximum would support an intermediate optimum; a linear or flat fit, or a maximum only at the boundary of the selected window, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A quadratic on 13 points is easy to overfit.

The 13-bot subset was constrained to a gyration window after a linear fit misbehaved, and the points are not public.

Edge similarity depends on how the scratch centerline was drawn.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.1
discriminating power: 0.28
data existence: 0.14
analysis feasibility: 0.18
operationalizability: 0.84
